Insert or update with ON CONFLICT

PostgreSQL 19.0

Use an upsert when a key should identify the same record across repeated writes.

Open interactive lesson

On this page

  • Define the conflict key
  • Choose whether to skip a conflict
  • Official references

Define the conflict key

The existing enrollment for student 1 and course 1 has a two-column primary key. ON CONFLICT finds that row. EXCLUDED.enrolled_on is the date proposed by INSERT. ROLLBACK restores the original date after the example.

BEGIN;
INSERT INTO enrollments (student_id, course_id, enrolled_on)
VALUES (1, 1, DATE '2026-01-08')
ON CONFLICT (student_id, course_id) DO UPDATE
SET enrolled_on = EXCLUDED.enrolled_on
RETURNING student_id, course_id, enrolled_on;
ROLLBACK;

Choose whether to skip a conflict

Use DO NOTHING when an existing record should be kept as it is. A skipped row is not returned by RETURNING. Use DO UPDATE when you have a defined rule for changing the existing record.

INSERT INTO enrollments (student_id, course_id, enrolled_on)
VALUES (1, 1, DATE '2026-01-10')
ON CONFLICT (student_id, course_id) DO NOTHING
RETURNING student_id, course_id, enrolled_on;
